title: UNNEST drops a NULL list and an empty one; parallel UNNESTs pad with NULL
verdict: no row for `[]` or NULL; `[NULL]` gives a NULL row
description: `unnest(l)` in the select list and a lateral `unnest(l)` give one row per element and no row for an empty or NULL list; `[NULL]` gives one row with NULL. A `LEFT JOIN unnest(l) ON TRUE` keeps those rows with NULL. Two `unnest`s in one select list run in parallel, the shorter padded with NULL (`unnest([1, 2]), unnest([7])` gives `(1, 7), (2, NULL)`), and an empty one pads entirely.
reference: `UNNEST` gives one row per element and none for an empty list or NULL (sverify's own extension, reference-semantics.md, Nested). DuckDB's SQL is a lateral `UNNEST(l) WITH ORDINALITY` (docs/nested-values.md).
